definition: A legal writ ordering that a detained person be brought before a court so a judge can decide whether their imprisonment is lawful.
origin: From Latin habeas corpus, literally "you shall have the body," the opening words of the medieval writ commanding a jailer to produce a prisoner in court. definition: The organised, ongoing conduct of illegal business activity, such as extortion or fraud, typically carried out through a criminal enterprise.
origin: From American English racket (a noisy, fraudulent scheme), whose own origin is uncertain, possibly echoing the din of a rowdy party or scam. The term hardened in early 20th-century Chicago slang, where a "racket" meant a criminal business run under the guise of legitimate trade, and "racketeering" named the ongoing practice of running one.
